title: Tenant-aware regression watchdog with customer data sovereignty controls
creator: Marco Liu
description: Build a tenant-aware regression monitoring workflow that runs customer-specific eval suites in isolated environments and enforces strict data sovereignty and encryption controls. The feature must integrate with model/config change events, surface per-tenant quality deltas in the Console, and provide automated guardrails (alerts, rollbacks, or staged rollouts) while ensuring no customer data leaves their VPC or on-prem footprint unless explicitly permitted.
background: Customers on Dedicated and Private deployments have been requesting stronger guarantees that evals used to measure regressions run against tenant-owned test sets without leaking prompts or outputs. Current platform evals run in a shared managed environment and lack per-tenant KMS scoping and end-to-end isolation. Several P1 incidents highlighted risks: accidental exposure of eval inputs in aggregated dashboards and lack of automated per-tenant gating when a model change caused measurable quality regressions for a single large account.
scope: Design and ship a 'tenant-aware regression watchdog' that: 1) Accepts customer-provided eval suites or selects curated tenant-profiled suites; 2) Executes evals in tenant-isolated compute (VPC or on-prem agent) or against encrypted buckets with customer-managed KMS; 3) Ties execution to model/config change hooks and returns a per-tenant quality delta within SLA; 4) Surfaces results in Console with RBAC and encrypted-at-rest storage; 5) Provides configurable guardrails (threshold alerts, auto-block deploy, canary with rollback).
out_of_scope: Building an entirely new eval authoring UI (we will initially accept uploads and API-based suite registration), long-term MLOps integrations for continuous training pipelines, and providing default customer-owned on-prem hardware (only agent and orchestration).
success_criteria: Per-tenant eval run completes within 30 minutes after model/config change for suites up to 2k examples
Console shows tenant-scoped quality delta and historical trend with access limited by RBAC
If quality regression exceeds configured threshold, the platform can block automatic rollout and create a rollback job
Eval inputs, outputs, and metrics stored under customer KMS with no plaintext replication in Redwood shared stores by default
Initial beta with 3 pilot customers on Dedicated/Private completes with feedback loop and documented runbooks
acceptance_criteria: API: customers can register an eval suite via API or upload ZIP containing testcases and metadata
Privacy: platform supports binding an eval run to a customer KMS key and VPC/isolation mode
Triggering: model or config change events (model version pin, runtime config change, quantization profile update) trigger per-tenant eval jobs automatically
Visibility: per-tenant eval result card appears in Console within 45 minutes of job start, includes pass/fail, normalized score delta, and sample failures
Guardrails: Console allows configuring threshold action: notify / block deploy / initiate rollback / require manual approval
Audit: every eval run emits an immutable audit record with timestamp, agent id, job id, and non-sensitive metric summary
Security review: solution passes security review and threat modeling for data exfiltration vectors
technical_notes: Execution modes: (A) In-cloud isolated: eval runs in a fenced tenant project with encryption at rest using customer or Redwood KMS; (B) VPC connector: eval runner in customer's VPC with short-lived credentials; (C) On-prem agent: customer hosts runner and posts encrypted metrics. Use streaming metric aggregation to avoid storing raw outputs in Redwood controllers. Tie into model-change webhook system; add a new 'tenant-eval' job type to job-scheduler. Metrics should be computed locally and only metrics+non-sensitive failure examples (redacted) may be sent back by default.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design + security review (2 sprints). Phase 1: Internal demo and 3 pilot customers on Dedicated (4 sprints). Phase 2: Console UX polish, RBAC integration, beta expansion (3 sprints). Phase 3: General availability with docs and runbooks. Feature flag gated by customer tier and region.
risks: Metric leakage: improperly redacted failure examples could leak PII
Latency: running per-tenant evals on every model change could increase deployment time for high-frequency teams
Operational cost: executing large suites for many tenants adds compute costs; need budget/rate limits
Complexity of KMS integration across public clouds and customer-managed HSMs
open_questions: Should we require customers to provide CI-friendly pass/fail thresholds or provide default thresholds per workload type?
What's the max suite size we guarantee in SLA before throttling or charging?
How much sample failure data may we display in aggregate dashboards without violating isolation?
Do we ship a lightweight eval runner binary for on-prem or rely on containers only?
